When you are asked to simplify a rational expression you should begin by factoring both the numerator and the denominator completely, then cancel any factor that appears in both, remembering that you may only cancel factors and never terms, and that any value of the variable which would make the original denominator equal to zero must be excluded from the domain even if the factor causing it cancels during simplification, which is a detail that many students overlook when they first meet these problems and which examiners test deliberately year after year, so it is worth writing the excluded values down at the moment you factor rather than trying to recover them at the end, because by then the expression in front of you no longer contains the factor that caused the exclusion and there is nothing left on the page to remind you that it was ever there, which is exactly the trap the question was built around in the first place.
